title: Control Plane governance extras: SIEM export, saved approval preferences and privacy-safe usage events
summary: After the unified decision audit exists, add a per-org audit-core exporter (batches with gzip, bounded queue that drops the oldest with a lag metric, retry ladder then a DLQ, encrypted credentials, destination host allowlist, test delivery). Store browser approval preferences in Control Plane user settings (approval_mode, per-origin rules, revision, revision-checked PATCH) so the Model Plane risk gate can record decided_by=saved_user_permission. Add typed, enum-only product usage events (takeover, approval requested and resolved, tool called with terminal status) forwarded server-side to the Control Plane usage stream.
whyItMatters: SIEM export is an enterprise procurement checkbox once audit is unified; saved approvals cut approval fatigue on repeat sites; usage events show which browser features users and agents actually use, to prioritise parity work. All are invisible to day-one users.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Firecrawl for SIEM (per-org batches of 200 events or 1 s, bounded 100k queue dropping the oldest, retry ladder 5 s to 30 min then a DLQ kept 7 days, destination host allowlist) and Codex for preferences and usage events (revisioned server document mirrored locally; typed events without URLs)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: SIEM 1 of 4 (unique); approval preferences 1 of 4 (unique); product usage analytics 2 of 4 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An audit-core consumer per org with {kind, endpoint allowlist, encrypted credentials}; user browser_prefs with If-Match revision read by the risk gate; an analytics event catalogue whose properties are enums and counts only, disabled for ZDR orgs and on user opt-out, with no third-party script in the page.

verevonToday.gap: SIEM export is absent (audit-core persists verevon.audit.v2.> and usage events with no export integration, and Quarry does not publish to audit-core subjects). Saved approval preferences and product usage events are unknown: a limited grep found no analytics client (posthog, statsig, mixpanel, amplitude, sentry) in the SPA source or gateway manifest, and no browser approval-preference setting was located. Not checked: Model Plane approve-for-session persistence.

approach: Control Plane: audit-core exporter, user settings schema for browser_prefs, usage event ingestion. Model Plane: risk gate reads preferences but never auto-approves ZDR-forbidden or sensitive one-shot actions; saved rules are origin-scoped and expiring. Frontend Plane: a small typed event module posting to a gateway endpoint, suppressed under ZDR.
risks: Exporting URLs for ZDR orgs and destination SSRF (allowlist hosts); saved permissions silently widening authority; third-party analytics conflicting with ZDR and sovereignty positioning.

verevon.exactGap: None of the three deliverables exists. audit-core is a durable consumer of verevon.audit.v2.> and verevon.usage.v2.> with append-only audit_events and usage_events tables and a pull API (GET /v1/audit, /v1/usage) but no push exporter, destination config or delivery queue, and Quarry publishes no audit events (only Model Plane session-core publishes tool_action). User settings are generic per-category rows with no revision field and no browser category, and the browser decided event leaves decided_by empty (browser_events.rs:148,574,612), so no saved-approval path exists. No analytics client appears in the SPA package.json or gateway Cargo.toml, and usage_events holds billable usage, not product events.

verevon.constraints: Control Plane owns audit, usage and user settings, so the exporter and preferences store live there; Model Plane may read preferences only through a Control authority call and must never auto-approve sensitive one-shot actions or anything ZDR forbids. Exported audit must carry no page content for ZDR orgs and the destination needs a host allowlist (SSRF) and encrypted credentials. Saved approvals must be origin-scoped, expiring and never widen a Space or owner-plane ACL. Third-party analytics in the SPA conflicts with the ZDR and sovereignty positioning.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the bundle. (1) SIEM export stands alone as an audit-core consumer with per-org destination, allowlist, retry then DLQ and test delivery; an S interim is to let customers pull GET /v1/audit with a service token. (2) Saved approval preferences duplicate F-t2-032's per-origin consent store: put them in Control Plane user settings (new browser category with a revision) and merge the work into F-t2-032 instead of building a second store; the BrowserActionDecided sink must carry the real decider before decided_by can say saved_user_permission. (3) Product usage events should not add a SPA analytics client: emit enum-only counters server-side from the gateway or execution-core into the existing usage v2 subject, suppressed for ZDR orgs. Quarry must first publish decision audit (F-t2-036) before an export is meaningful for browser actions.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M as a bundle: the SIEM exporter alone is M-L (queue, retry, DLQ, encrypted credentials, allowlist), the preferences store is shared with F-t2-032 and the usage events need a new server-side path.
verevon.verdictReason: All three parts are absent and the item correctly sits late, but it bundles unrelated work, double-counts the approval-preference store that F-t2-032 needs, and proposes a SPA analytics path that conflicts with ZDR; rewrite as a SIEM-export item plus a merge note into F-t2-032 and a server-side-only usage-counter note.
